newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-UBS unit charged in Jersey.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UBS unit charged in Jersey.

text.p: A wholly owned subsidiary of Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said on Tuesday police in the British Channel island of Jersey had charged the company and one of its officers under a prevention of fraud law.
"The charges against the bank are being investigated and subject to the investigation will be contested," Zurich-based UBS subsidiary Cantrade Privatbank AG, said in a statement.
"A plea of not guilty will be entered at the appropriate time," it added.
Hans Fischer, chairman of the Cantrade group executive board, said the charges were related to losses at several investment funds deposited with Cantrade by an outside fund management group.
Fischer said Cantrade in Jersey had been the depository bank for the investment funds, which were run on behalf of about 90 investors by TTS Management.
Fischer said the investors had filed a civil action against Cantrade, TTS Management and a foreign exchange trader working under mandate to TTS, Robert Young.
"The issue in the both the civil and police action is to what extent Cantrade is responsible for the losses," Fischer told Reuters.
"The trader concerned, Robert Young, who was charged in August, is not and has never been an employee of Cantrade," the bank statement said.
Fischer estimated the losses to the investment funds in the period between 1988 and 1993 at about $10 to $12 million.
"Cantrade is defending the civil action but will meet any claims which are legally justified," it said.
The Cantrade group had capital of 455.1 million francs ($363 million) at the end of 1995, including about 60 million Swiss francs at Jersey legal entity Cantrade Private bank Switzerland (C.I.) Ltd.
Cantrade said the management team of subsidiary Cantrade Jersey had been changed since the alleged offences took place.
"The officer charged has been suspended pending the resolution of the charges against him," it said.
Fischer named the officer as Peter Stoneman, manager of the Jersey unit and not a member of the executive board. Fischer said Stoneman's suspension was routine in such cases.

The Cantrade Privatbank Group comprises the Zurich bank and subsidiaries in Geneva, Lugano and Jersey. It posted a group net profit of 73.1 million Swiss francs in 1995 and cash flow of 140.7 million.
Cantrade said it was treating this matter extremely seriously and was committed to complying with all relevant laws and standards of best practice.
"The bank is sound, well-capitalised and will meet all its obligations as they fall due," the statement said. ($1=1.2530 Swiss Franc)
